parsed.elsewhere_quote: Since $S_0 = \emptyset$, the function $g$ never takes the value $0$.  Together with §3 this forces $g(x) \equiv c$ for the positive constant $c$.  Thus $f(x) = x + c$
parsed.explanation: The listed dichotomy is indeed incomplete: after "at most one positive value", the possibilities are V={0}, V={c}, V={0,c}, and the pure case V={c} is not listed. But this omission costs nothing: §4–§6 do not merely refute the mixed case, they prove S_0 = ∅ outright (via (12) and the covering of (0,∞) by intervals of radius c around the orbit u+nc), and §7 then concludes g ≡ c, which is exactly the omitted case and yields f(x)=x+c. The identity case g ≡ 0 (c=0) is separately noted. So L5.5's content — constant difference for all x, fixed points excluded when c>0 — is established as written; the flaw is only in the labelling of cases.
